topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the context for the cancer lecture series, and outlines the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Origins of Cancer: Genetics, Random Mutations, and Epidemiological Patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore fundamental cancer biology, debating the relative roles of endogenous mutation, bad luck, environmental factors, and geographic variations in disease incidence.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the role of viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections in driving malignancies, highlighted by the detailed case study of Burkitt lymphoma and Epstein-Barr virus.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe specific carcinogens—such as aflatoxin, UV light, benzo[a]pyrene, TCDD, and aromatic amines—and the biochemical and metabolic mechanisms through which they induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumour Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics differentiate cancer initiation from promotion, explaining how non-mutagenic stimuli like asbestos, phorbol esters, and life-stage tissue proliferation enable tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying Carcinogens and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the experimental and epidemiological tools used to demonstrate carcinogenicity—including mutational signatures, biobanks, animal models, and the Ames test—and conclude with risk-benefit assessment.
